brief: GS Sales & Trading's morning digest reports China's industrial profits accelerating to +14.4% y/y in September (from +4.2%) as AI-driven manufacturing offsets weak domestic demand, and South Korea's Q3 GDP beating estimates (+1% vs +0.8%) on an AI chip export and investment boom, though a consumption contraction complicates the rate-hike path. The BoJ's core inflation gauge surged to 3.2% y/y, the highest in three years and well above its 2% target. French consumer confidence hit a 13-year low on a bond selloff and protests. Politically: Brazil's Bolsonaro dropped his election challenge, turning attention to whether Lula reins in spending as fiscal strain mounts; China will send envoys to the Middle East to help prevent a resumption of US-Israeli strikes on Iran; the US and Canada are negotiating easing tariffs on Canadian steel and autos; Israelis vote today in a razor-thin Netanyahu-Eisenkot race. Separately, PE funds are racing to extend loans against a $300bn 2028 debt wall as rates rise, and hedge fund gross leverage stays elevated (312%, 96th percentile) even as net leverage fell to a one-year low (47%), reflecting defensive positioning without de-grossing. The note also carries about twenty sell-side rating actions and the day's earnings/econ calendar.

cards.claim: The BoJ's core inflation gauge (consumer prices excluding fresh food and special factors) rose 3.2% year-over-year in September, the highest in three years and well above the BoJ's 2% target.

cards.claim: French consumer confidence fell to a 13-year low in October as households grappled with a bond selloff and violent protests.
